key_insight: During nanoscratch of 316H stainless steel, the local stress state selects a sequential martensitic path of γ → ε → α′, with hydrostatic compression favoring ε and shear enabling ε → α′.
engineering_relevance: The results show how contact pressure and sliding govern tribolayer formation and galling-related surface hardening, which is directly relevant to wear-resistant alloy design and tribological modeling.
method: In-situ synchrotron X-ray nanodiffractometry during nanoscratch
Finite element modeling of the subsurface strain/stress field
Spatial mapping of martensite phase evolution beneath a single asperity
evidence_signal: The abstract reports spatially resolved experimental maps combined with FEM interpretation, linking phase distributions to local hydrostatic compression and shear during scratching.
watch_item: The findings come from a single-asperity nanoscratch geometry, so direct transfer to multi-asperity or real-service tribological contacts may require additional validation.
paper_title: Spatially resolved in-situ characterisation of competing martensitic transformation pathways during nanoscratch in 316H Stainless Steel
